Article 9

1. Women who become victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services and continuous handling.
2. Continuous handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out up to the rehabilitation stage.
3. Continuous handling as referred to in paragraph (2) can be carried out by individuals, groups, regional government institutions, and/or non-governmental institutions.

Article 12

1. The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the Region as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.
2. The membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, the community, universities and/or community organizations.
3. Provisions regarding the establishment and membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be stipulated by a Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER V

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 15

1. The Regional Government shall conduct monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and protection of women.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the Region.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies, programs and activities implementing policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and protection of women.
4. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be carried out from the planning stage, up to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women for the current year.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karawang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Karawang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration who lead the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Empowerment of Women is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Task force is a semi-permanent working group, consisting of related regional apparatus work units, community, universities, and/or community organizations chaired by the Regional Secretary, who is given additional tasks within a certain period of time, to implement certain programs/activities in the field of empowerment and protection of women.
9. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, community and state), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.

Article 16

1. The Regional Government shall evaluate the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the empowerment and protection of women at the end of each fiscal year in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.

CHAPTER IV

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 14

1. The community may participate in the implementation of the empowerment and protection of women.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups and/or social community organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may take the form of:a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 8

1. Empowerment of women is implemented to mengingkatkan the position, [eran and quality of Women in family, community, and national life.
2. Empowerment of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed so that Women:a. Obtain their opportunities and rights as human beings;
b. Are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities;danc. Have equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER VII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 18

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all Regional laws and regulations relating to the empowerment and protection of women shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to the provisions of this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER III

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 10

The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of institutions for Empowerment and Protection of Women in the Region.
